page: Amazon Web Services g5.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for graphics-intensive and machine learning workloads. It features 96 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 7R32 processors running at 3.3 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture with 48 physical cores. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it bundles four NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs with a combined total of 89 GB of VRAM.

Local storage consists of 3800 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in large language model (LLM) inference, achieving top 10% results in prompt processing and text generation across 135M, 7B, and 70B models. While single-core CPU performance is categorized as poor (bottom 10%) in stress-ng tests, multi-core CPU performance is average, and Passmark CPU encryption tests reach top-tier levels. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is strong, though large block read and write speeds remain average.

The hardware configuration presents a clear tradeoff between moderate single-core CPU execution and exceptional parallel GPU processing. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is high for workloads that can leverage the dense multi-GPU setup and local NVMe storage, rather than relying purely on raw single-threaded CPU speed. This makes the g5.24xlarge highly suitable for LLM inference, ray tracing, image processing, and high-throughput cryptographic operations.
description: Amazon Web Services g5.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring 96 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 7R32 processors at 3.3 GHz, 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and four NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs with 89 GB of total VRAM. It includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. While single-core CPU benchmarks are relatively weak, the instance delivers top-tier performance in LLM inference across small, medium, and large models, alongside strong results in ray tracing, image processing, and cryptographic operations. This hardware profile offers high resource density for parallel computing, making it a cost-efficient choice for GPU-heavy workloads. It is highly suited for machine learning inference, graphics rendering, and data-intensive applications.
